title: Asthma: stepwise therapy and the exacerbation

source.citation: Written for Blackout, 2026-09-13. Based on the GINA strategy report. Not tied to an article; review before trusting.

questions.q: Under GINA, what is the preferred reliever for a newly diagnosed adult with mild asthma?
questions.why: Salbutamol-only treatment is no longer recommended at any step because it leaves the airway inflammation untreated and is linked to exacerbations and deaths.

questions.q: A patient on as-needed ICS-formoterol has symptoms most days. What is the next step?
questions.a: Low-dose ICS-formoterol as maintenance and reliever
questions.why: Maintenance and reliever therapy uses one inhaler for both jobs, which simplifies adherence. Medium-dose maintenance is the step after that.

questions.q: Over the past four weeks, which findings mean asthma is not well controlled?
a: Daytime symptoms more than twice a week
Reliever use more than twice a week
d: A peak flow at 85% of best
questions.why: One or two of the four means partly controlled; three or four means uncontrolled. Reliever use for prevention before exercise does not count.

questions.q: Before stepping up asthma treatment, what should be checked first?
questions.a: Inhaler technique, adherence, and modifiable risk factors
questions.why: Most apparent treatment failure is poor technique or missed doses. Comorbid rhinitis, reflux, smoking and beta blockers are looked for at the same time.

questions.q: In an asthma exacerbation, what oxygen saturation is targeted?
questions.why: The lower range of 88% to 92% belongs to COPD. High-flow uncontrolled oxygen in asthma has been associated with worse outcomes.

questions.q: What course of oral prednisone is standard for an adult asthma exacerbation?
questions.a: 40 to 50 mg daily for 5 to 7 days
d: 60 mg daily for 14 days with a taper
options: 40 to 50 mg daily for 5 to 7 days
60 mg daily for 14 days with a taper
questions.why: No taper is needed for courses under two weeks. Systemic steroids within the first hour reduce admissions and relapse.

questions.q: A severe exacerbation is not responding to repeated bronchodilators and steroids in the first hour. Which intravenous therapy is added?
questions.why: A single 2 g infusion over 20 minutes reduces admissions in severe cases. Antibiotics are not given unless there is evidence of bacterial infection.

questions.q: A peak flow below what percentage of predicted or personal best marks a severe exacerbation?
questions.why: Between 50% and 75% is moderate. Inability to complete sentences, a heart rate over 120 and a silent chest are the clinical markers that matter more than the number.

questions.q: On spirometry, what confirms reversible airflow obstruction?
questions.a: FEV1 rises by 12% or more and at least 200 mL after a bronchodilator
d: A fall in FVC after a bronchodilator
questions.why: Normal spirometry between episodes does not exclude asthma; the test is repeated when symptomatic, or a bronchial challenge test is used.

questions.q: After how long of good control should stepping down treatment be considered?
questions.why: Step down one step at a time, not during a respiratory infection or travel, and never to salbutamol alone.

questions.q: Severe asthma remains uncontrolled on high-dose ICS-LABA with good technique and adherence. Which add-on comes before maintenance oral steroids?
questions.a: A biologic chosen by phenotype, such as an anti-IL-5 for eosinophilic disease
questions.why: Long-acting muscarinic antagonist is the other step 5 add-on. Maintenance oral steroids are the last resort because of their cumulative harm.

questions.q: What simple instruction reduces oral thrush from inhaled corticosteroids?
questions.a: Rinse the mouth and spit after each dose, and use a spacer with a metered-dose inhaler
d: Use the inhaler only at night
questions.why: A spacer also improves lung deposition from a metered-dose inhaler, which is why technique is checked at every visit.
